mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4% indicates labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 4% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases, it may indicate a tight labor market with high competition for jobs, which could positively impact equity markets through increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS growth and UNRATE increase occur but the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth during a late-cycle expansion may signal supply chain constraints or reduced business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth slows in a late-cycle expansion but the S&P 500 continues to show positive 60-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which could lead to positive S&P 500 returns as companies experience higher revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: If real sales increase but the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth below 1% year-over-year may indicate supply chain issues or reduced production, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is below 1% YoY but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with strong GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate an accommodative monetary policy supporting economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low and GDPC1 grows but the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4% in a tightening cycle but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns, this hypothesis is rejected.
